questions.question: Six friends have an average height of 144 cm. A boy with a height of 150 cm leaves the group. Find the new average height.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average height of six friends = 144 cm

Height of the boy leaving the group = 150 cm

**Concept Used:**

When one member leaves a group, the new average can be found by recalculating the sum of the remaining members and dividing by the new number of members.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of heights of all members = Average height × Number of members

New average height = (Sum of heights of all members - Height of the boy leaving) / New number of members

**Calculation:**

Sum of heights of six friends = 144 cm × 6

⇒ 144 × 6 = 864 cm

Sum of heights after the boy leaves = 864 cm - 150 cm

⇒ 864 - 150 = 714 cm

New number of members = 6 - 1 = 5

New average height = 714 cm / 5

⇒ 714 / 5 = 142.8 cm

**∴ The new average height is 142.8 cm.**

questions.question: A and B can complete a work alone in 20 days and 60 days respectively. They began the work together but A left the work after some days and B completed the remaining work in 12 days. After how many days from the beginning A left the work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(20, 60) = 60 units.

Efficiency: A = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 units/day, B = 60 ÷ 60 = 1 unit/day.

Work done by B alone in the last 12 days = 12 × 1 = 12 units.

Remaining work done by A and B together from the beginning = 60 − 12 = 48 units.

Days A and B worked together = 48 ÷ (3 + 1) = 12 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A alone to complete the work = 20 days

Time taken by B alone to complete the work = 60 days

Time taken by B to complete the remaining work = 12 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time Taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work completed by B alone in the last 12 days = Efficiency of B × Days = 1 × 12 = 12 units

⇒ Remaining work to be completed by A and B together = Total Work − Work done by B

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 12 = 48 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and B = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day

⇒ Number of days A and B worked together initially = Remaining work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Days A and B worked together = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 days

This means A worked for 12 days from the beginning before leaving the work.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work & Efficiency Trick

Total work is universally taken as the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of individual completion times. Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken.

Alternate Days Working

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the work done in a complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 persons) and scale it up to reach the closest multiple near the total work.

Work & Wages Distribution

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the total units of work completed by each individual. If they work for the same duration, wages are directly distributed based on their efficiencies.

questions.question: Marked price of a chair is Rs. 5000. After giving two successive discounts of 10 percent and x percent, the chair is sold for Rs. 3150. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price of a chair = Rs. 5000

First discount = 10%

Second discount = x%

Selling price after discounts = Rs. 3150

**Concept:**

Successive discounts are applied one after the other on the remaining amount after each discount.

**Formula Used:**

Final Price = Marked Price × (1 - First Discount/100) × (1 - Second Discount/100)

**Calculation:**

Final Price = 5000 × (1 - 10/100) × (1 - x/100)

⇒ 3150 = 5000 × 0.9 × (1 - x/100)

⇒ 3150 = 4500 × (1 - x/100)

⇒ 3150/4500 = 1 - x/100

⇒ 0.7 = 1 - x/100

⇒ x/100 = 1 - 0.7

⇒ x/100 = 0.3

⇒ x = 0.3 × 100

⇒ x = 30

**∴ The value of x is 30 percent.**

questions.question: The ratio of copper and zinc in brass is 25 : 12. How much amount of copper will be there in 370 kg of brass?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total parts in the ratio = 25 (Copper) + 12 (Zinc) = 37 parts.

37 parts → 370 kg of brass.

1 part → 370 ÷ 37 = 10 kg.

Amount of copper (25 parts) = 25 × 10 = 250 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 250 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Ratio of Copper to Zinc = 25 : 12

⇒ Total quantity of brass = 370 kg

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the amount of copper be 25x and the amount of zinc be 12x.

⇒ Total weight of the mixture = 25x + 12x = 37x

⇒ It is given that the total weight of brass is 370 kg.

⇒ 37x = 370

⇒ x = 370 ÷ 37 = 10

⇒ Amount of copper in the mixture = 25x = 25 × 10 = 250 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 250 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dividing a Quantity in a Ratio

To divide a total quantity Q into a ratio a : b, the value of the first component is calculated as (a ÷ (a + b)) × Q, and the second component is calculated as (b ÷ (a + b)) × Q.

Proportion

When two ratios are set equal to each other (such as a : b = c : d), they are said to be in proportion. In any true proportion, the product of the extremes equals the product of the means (a × d = b × c).

Compound Ratio

For two or more given ratios like a : b and c : d, the compound ratio is formed by multiplying their respective antecedents together and their consequents together, resulting in ac : bd.

questions.question: If a certain sum of money becomes thrice of itself in 8 years 6 months at simple interest, then what will be the annual rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A certain sum of money becomes thrice itself in 8 years 6 months at simple interest.

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = Principal (P) × Rate (R) × Time (T) / 100

Total Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

**Calculation:**

Let the principal amount be P.

Given, the total amount becomes thrice of itself, so A = 3P.

Simple Interest (SI) = A - P = 3P - P = 2P

Time (T) = 8 years 6 months = 8.5 years

Using the formula for simple interest:

SI = P × R × T / 100

⇒ 2P = P × R × 8.5 / 100

⇒ 2 = R × 8.5 / 100

⇒ R = 2 × 100 / 8.5

⇒ R = 23.52%

**∴ The annual rate of interest is approximately 23.52%.**

questions.question: If 25 is subtracted from a number, then number becomes 50 percent of itself. What is the number?
questions.solution:

x - 25 = 0.5x

**Concept Used:**

To find the number, we need to solve the linear equation for x.

**Calculation:**

x - 25 = 0.5x

⇒ x - 0.5x = 25

⇒ 0.5x = 25

⇒ x = 25 / 0.5

⇒ x = 50

**∴ The number is 50.**

questions.question: A person covers first 11 km in 60 minutes and next 22 km in 30 minutes. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

First distance = 11 km

Time for first distance = 60 minutes

Second distance = 22 km

Time for second distance = 30 minutes

**Concept:**

Average speed is calculated by dividing the total distance by the total time taken.

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

**Calculation:**

Total Distance = 11 km + 22 km

⇒ Total Distance = 33 km

Total Time = 60 minutes + 30 minutes

⇒ Total Time = 90 minutes

Convert total time from minutes to hours:

⇒ Total Time = 90/60 hours

⇒ Total Time = 1.5 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 33 km / 1.5 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 22 km/hr

**∴ The average speed for the whole journey is 22 km/hr.**

questions.question: If selling price of a table is 25 percent of its cost price, then what is the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = 25% of Cost Price (CP)

**Concept Used:**

To find the loss percentage, we need to determine the difference between Cost Price (CP) and Selling Price (SP) and then express it as a percentage of the Cost Price.

**Formula used:**

Loss Percentage = [(CP - SP) / CP] × 100%

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

Selling Price (SP) = 25% of CP

⇒ SP = 25% of 100 = 25 units

Loss = CP - SP

⇒ Loss = 100 - 25 = 75 units

Loss Percentage = (Loss / CP) × 100

⇒ Loss Percentage = (75 / 100) × 100

⇒ Loss Percentage = 75%

**∴ The loss percentage is 75%.**
